item.title: Itoshima Oyster Huts (Kaki-goya) — Guide
item.description: Each winter, the fishing harbours of the Itoshima Peninsula west of Fukuoka come alive with kaki-goya — oyster huts, simple covered structures set up right by the water where you grill and eat freshly harvested local oysters. Seasonal from around autumn to spring, these no-frills huts are a beloved local tradition: you sit at a table with a charcoal or gas grill, order oysters by the basket straight from the nearby beds, and cook them yourself until they pop open, eating them hot with a squeeze of citrus, soy or ponzu.

item.title: Itoshima Peninsula and Futamigaura Beach — Guide
item.description: The Itoshima Peninsula, a short drive west of Fukuoka city, has become one of the region’s most popular getaways — a relaxed stretch of coastline mixing beaches, surf, farm produce and a thriving scene of stylish seaside cafes, bakeries and craft studios. Its most photogenic sight is Futamigaura, where a pair of sacred ‘married rocks’ (meoto-iwa) linked by a sacred rope stand in the sea beside a striking white torii gate, framing spectacular sunsets over the water.
